analytics.disabled_reason: The canonical GitHub Pages publication has no same-origin server runtime. The browser and Python aggregate collector now share one tested event contract, but production collection remains off until deployment, notice and host/proxy logging gates are verified.
enable_procedure: Deploy analytics/collector.py behind HTTPS with the publication and /api/analytics/events on the same origin; GitHub Pages alone cannot run this Python service.

Verify host/proxy logging and the privacy notice. Configure collector enablement, public origin and an external-to-repository database. Confirm /health and a synthetic end-to-end test in an isolated test database, never the campaign ledger.

Record runtime_selected, endpoint_deployed and privacy_notice_approved in data/analytics-plan.json. Set its collection.enabled and data/config.json analytics.enabled together; set analytics.endpoint to /api/analytics/events.
Run all build, contract and privacy tests and review the generated privacy notice before publishing. Do not claim collection is live until a real deployed request is accepted.
never_recorded: cookie or any persistent reader identifier
order value or anything about what the reader bought
analytics.policy_basis: Program Policies §3(e) requires accurate technology disclosures; §6(s) prohibits artificially generated clicks. Measurement does not trigger affiliate navigation: it observes trusted reader activations without blocking them. Page views and reading events have their own definitions. Application aggregation is not proof of a unique person or a purchase.
